'''William John Greenstreet''' (1861–1930) was an English [[mathematician]] who was editor of ''[[The Mathematical Gazette]]'' for more than thirty years.{{sfn | Macaulay|Neville|Pendlebury|Spender|1930|p=181 }}

== Life and work ==
Greenstreet was son of a Royal Artillery's Sergeant. He was educated at [[Southwark]] and he entered [[St John's College, Cambridge]] in 1879, graduating there in 1883. Then he was mathematics professor in different schools in [[Framlingham]], [[East Riding of Yorkshire|East Riding]] and [[Cardiff]] before he became Head Master at [[Marling School]] in 1891. In 1910 he retired to [[Burghfield Common]] with the intention of devoting to literary work.{{sfn | Macaulay|Neville|Pendlebury|Spender|1930|p=182 }}

Greenstreet was founding member of the [[Mathematical Association]]{{dubious|reason=The association began under a different name in 1871, when Greenstreet would have been only 10.|date=October 2018}} and he started the Association's Library given a large collection of books.{{sfn | Goodstein | 1974 | p=100 }}
